[[File:Trofeo UEFA Champions League.jpg|thumb|upright|right|UEFA Champions League trophy]]
The [[UEFA Champions League]], known as the European Cup before 1992, is an [[association football]] competition contested since 1956. Spanish manager [[José Villalonga]] led [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] to success in the inaugural [[1956 European Cup final|final in 1956]] and repeated the feat the following season. The competition became the UEFA Champions League in [[1992–93 UEFA Champions League|1992]],<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/ | title = History |website=UEFA.com | publisher = Union of European Football Associations | access-date = 5 March 2008 | date = 2 July 2007 | archive-date = 6 December 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151206212222/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/index.html | url-status = live }}</ref> with Belgian [[Raymond Goethals]] leading French club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] to success that season.

[[Carlo Ancelotti]] has won a record five titles with [[AC Milan]] and Real Madrid. [[Bob Paisley]], [[Zinedine Zidane]], [[Pep Guardiola]] and [[Luis Enrique]] have won the tournament three times. Paisley led [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to three titles in five seasons, Zidane won three consecutive titles with Real Madrid, and Luis Enrique led [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] to two consecutive titles and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] to one title. Sixteen other managers have won the competition twice. Only seven managers have won the title with two clubs: Ancelotti with Milan in [[2003 UEFA Champions League final|2003]] and [[2007 UEFA Champions League final|2007]] and Real Madrid in [[2014 UEFA Champions League final|2014]], [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|2022]], and [[2024 UEFA Champions League final|2024]]; [[Ernst Happel]] with [[Feyenoord]] in [[1970 European Cup final|1970]] and [[Hamburger SV|Hamburg]] in [[1983 European Cup final|1983]]; [[Ottmar Hitzfeld]] with [[Borussia Dortmund]] in [[1997 UEFA Champions League final|1997]] and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in [[2001 UEFA Champions League final|2001]]; [[José Mourinho]] with [[FC Porto|Porto]] in [[2004 UEFA Champions League final|2004]] and [[Inter Milan]] in [[2010 UEFA Champions League final|2010]]; [[Jupp Heynckes]] with Real Madrid in [[1998 UEFA Champions League final|1998]] and Bayern Munich in [[2013 UEFA Champions League final|2013]]; Guardiola with Barcelona in [[2009 UEFA Champions League final|2009]] and [[2011 UEFA Champions League final|2011]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in [[2023 UEFA Champions League final|2023]]; and Luis Enrique with Barcelona in [[2015 UEFA Champions League final|2015]] and Paris Saint-Germain in [[2025 UEFA Champions League final|2025]] and [[2026 UEFA Champions League final|2026]]. Seven men have won the tournament both as a player and as a manager: [[Miguel Muñoz]], [[Giovanni Trapattoni]], [[Johan Cruyff]], [[Frank Rijkaard]], Ancelotti, Guardiola and Zidane.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50080/coach.html |title=Frank Rijkaard |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations|access-date=28 May 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080205090519/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club%3D50080/coach.html |archive-date=5 February 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| url = http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50080/coach.html| title = Josep Guardiola|website=UEFA.com| publisher = Union of European Football Associations| access-date = 28 May 2009| archive-date = 5 February 2008| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080205090519/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50080/coach.html| url-status = dead}}</ref>
